steps.say: The practice market, with Gus, your grown-up today. Everything here is practice. Let's learn what to do if you ever get lost.
Learn your address and your grown-up's phone number at home, and say them aloud to your grown-up. The game never asks for them. If you're lost, who may you tell them to?

choices.text: A police officer or a shop worker who is helping me

choices.why: Never online. Say them only to a safe grown-up who is helping you, like a police officer.

steps.done: Only to a safe grown-up who is helping you.

steps.say: Oh! You were looking at the toys, and now you can't see Gus. That's OK: it can happen to anyone. Here's what to do.
First: stop, and stay where you are. Your grown-up will come back to look for you here. Stand still.
steps.done: Staying put helps your grown-up find you.

lines.worker: A shop worker with a name badge: they work here.

steps.say: If your grown-up doesn't come, ask a safe grown-up: someone who works here with a name badge, a mum or dad with children, or a police officer. Find two.
steps.done: Those are safe grown-ups to ask.

lines.worker: A shop worker with a name badge.

steps.say: Find all three safe grown-ups to ask.
steps.done: All three, all by yourself.

steps.say: Touch the shop worker and say: "I'm lost." Stay with her, right here at her stall.
steps.done: She says: "Let's wait here together, and I'll call for your grown-up."

steps.say: Never go anywhere with anyone, even someone who says they'll help: a safe grown-up helps you right where you are. A man says "Come with me!" You...

choices.why: Never go off with anyone. Stay right where you are, with the shop worker.

steps.done: You stayed. That's just right.

steps.say: Gus is back! He came looking for you, and found you because you stayed put. A big hug.
Now the practice school. The bell rings: a fire drill! A drill is practice, so everyone knows what to do. Leave your things and follow your teacher.
Stop what you're doing, and stand in the line behind your teacher.
steps.done: In the line, nice and quiet.

steps.say: The drill: where do you go?
steps.done: In the line, by yourself.

steps.say: Follow your teacher calmly to the meeting point outside. Walk, don't run.
steps.done: At the meeting point. The teacher counts everyone: all here.

steps.say: Your favourite pencil is still inside. You...

choices.why: Never go back in: things can be replaced, and your teacher needs to see you.

steps.done: With your class, until the teacher says the drill is over.

steps.say: On the way home, you remember the way by things you see: landmarks. Which is a good landmark?

choices.why: Clouds move away! Pick things that stay: a bridge, a big tree, a shop sign.

steps.done: The red bridge: it stays where it is.

name_it.title: Stay, ask, follow
lines: Lost? Stop, and stay where you are: your grown-up will come back to look.
Ask a safe grown-up: a worker with a name badge, a parent with children, a police officer.
Never go off with anyone, even if they say they'll help.
A fire drill: leave your things and follow your teacher calmly to the meeting point.
name_it.source: the police's and child-safety charities' advice (NCMEC, Kidpower) and the fire and rescue services

little.try_real: Say your address to your grown-up now, and your grown-up's phone number: they'll tell you if it's right. Never type them into a game or a website. Then agree where you'd meet if you got separated in a shop.

sources.fact: If a child gets lost: stop and stay in one place, as their grown-up is usually close by and will come back; then ask a safe adult: uniformed police or security officers, or shop staff wearing name tags.
sources.source: NCMEC (the US missing children's organisation), child safety

sources.fact: Children who are lost can ask a mother or father with children for help, stay in the same place, and should never go off with anyone, even someone offering to help.
Children should learn their address and a parent's phone number by heart, to give to the police or a safe adult who is helping them.
In a fire drill: stop what you're doing, leave your belongings, follow your teacher calmly to the assembly point, stay with your class to be counted, and never go back in.
sources.source: the fire and rescue services, school fire drills (the London Fire Brigade)

You stopped to look at the kites, and now you can't see Gus. Stay calm: here's what to do.
First: stop and stay where you are. Your grown-up will come back to look for you here.
steps.done: Staying where you are is the quickest way to be found.

name_it.title: Stay, follow, find the way
lines: Lost: stay where you are and ask a safe grown-up. Never go off with anyone, even if they say they'll help.
A fire drill: leave your things, follow your teacher calmly to the meeting point, stay with your class.
The metro: change where the lines meet, tap your ticket, wait behind the yellow line.
A compass's red needle points north; landmarks help you find the way back.
name_it.source: the police's and child-safety charities' advice (NCMEC, Kidpower), the fire and rescue services, metro safety rules

middle.try_real: Say your address to your grown-up now, and their phone number: they'll tell you if it's right. Next time you ride a train or a metro, find the yellow line together, and where you'd change.

sources.fact: A lost child should stay where they are and ask a safe adult (police, security or shop staff with a name tag, a parent with children); they should insist on staying in the same place rather than going anywhere with anyone.
In a fire drill: leave belongings, line up, follow the teacher calmly to the assembly point, stay to be counted, never go back inside.
sources.source: the fire and rescue services, school fire drills (the London Fire Brigade)

sources.fact: Tbilisi's metro has 23 stations on two lines (the Akhmeteli-Varketili line and the Saburtalo line) that meet at Station Square, the one place to change.
sources.source: the Tbilisi metro (Tbilisi Transport Company); the Georgian encyclopedia

sources.fact: On a metro or railway platform, stand behind the yellow line until the train has stopped and the doors open; let people off first.
sources.source: metro and railway safety rules (Transport for London; the Tbilisi metro)

sources.fact: A magnetic compass's needle points to magnetic north; the cardinal points go round clockwise: north, east, south, west, with north-east, south-east, south-west and north-west between.
sources.source: Ordnance Survey, map reading and compass skills

The practice metro: the green line and the red line. {metro_where}

name_it.title: Plan, wait safely, take a bearing
lines: Plan the journey: change where the lines meet, and take the train towards the end station past yours.
Wait behind the yellow line; let people off first; mind the gap.
Separated from your group: stay put and ask the staff at a help point.
A map's key and grid squares (along, then up); a bearing: set it, turn to the needle, walk the arrow.
name_it.source: metro safety rules (Transport for London, the Tbilisi metro), Ordnance Survey's map and compass skills, and child-safety advice (NCMEC)

big.try_real: Say your address to your grown-up now, and their phone number. With a grown-up, plan a real journey on a map together, and try finding north with a compass or a phone's compass app.

sources.fact: Metro and railway safety: stand behind the yellow line until the train stops, let passengers off first, mind the gap; help points connect you to staff.
sources.source: metro and railway safety (Transport for London)

sources.fact: Tbilisi's metro has two lines, the Akhmeteli-Varketili line and the Saburtalo line, meeting at Station Square.
sources.source: the Tbilisi metro; the Georgian encyclopedia

sources.fact: Grid references: read along the bottom first, then up the side ('along the corridor, then up the stairs'); a map's key explains its symbols.

Walking on a bearing: set the bearing on the compass's dial at the direction-of-travel arrow, turn until the red needle sits in the orienting outline (red in the shed), then walk where the arrow points.
sources.source: Ordnance Survey, how to use a compass

sources.fact: If separated from a group or a grown-up in a public place, stay where you are and ask staff or police for help; know a grown-up's phone number by heart.
